judgments.rationale: The draft reading of paragraph (1) is independently complete and faithful to the source text. Paragraph (5) is a distinct provision separately addressed in another record, and another record or general provision does not incorporate its limitation into this statement. Incorporating paragraph (5) is an unnecessary and improper edit.

The proposal introduces inaccurate substantive requirements. The source grants permission to the agency ('may require') to request a written authorization specifically for discussion in an accompanying person's presence, whereas the proposal converts this into a mandatory duty ('must require') imposed on all individuals whether accompanied or unaccompanied.

The unchanged draft reading of C0000 accurately reflects the actor, mandatory force, request conditions, access rights, and permissive exception for accompanied review set forth in (d) and (d)(1), and it already meets the standard of an independently complete reading.

source_spans.quote: (d) Access to Records.— Each agency that maintains a system of rec­ords shall—

(1) upon request by any individual to gain access to his record or to any information pertaining to him which is contained in the system, permit him and upon his request, a person of his own choosing to accompany him, to review the record and have a copy made of all or any portion thereof in a form comprehensible to him, except that the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion of that individual’s record in the accompanying person’s presence;
(5) nothing in this section shall allow an individual access to any information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding.
